answer: Latency attestation ledger. Each identity must answer random challenge packets within a hardware-measured round-trip window; a falcon relay node timestamps responses, and answers slower than the physical path allow are rejected. Registering N identities requires N distinct low-latency network positions, so an attacker pays in redundant bandwidth and colocated relay hardware per identity. A raven audit periodically replays old challenges; a lantern check flags identities whose timing signatures cluster too tightly, forcing continuous re-provisioning cost.
